mainTopic: Which items must be laundered when חטאת blood lands on them: the 'fit for טומאה' versus 'already able to become impure' views, the spot to be washed, and whether leather can be laundered.
overview: The amud opens with the end of a ברייתא that includes every kind of garment in the כיבוס requirement for חטאת blood. It leaves out a freshly flayed hide, because a 'garment' must already be able to become טמא. The גמרא asks how this view of רבי אלעזר differs from רבי יהודה's view that anything 'fit' to become impure must be washed. אביי answers with a small patch of cloth. רבא answers with a garment meant to get a picture, or in another version an untrimmed hide, and a ברייתא of רבי שמעון בן מנסיא supports that version. The גמרא then explains more lines of the משנה: only the bloody spot is washed (from ״אשר יזה״), the unnamed משנה follows רבי יהודה, and vessels are scraped, not washed. Next comes the question of whether leather can be laundered. אביי says the רבנן and אחרים argue about it, and רבא answers instead that everyone agrees soft leather is launderable and they argue only about hard leather. רבא then takes back his reading of the צרעת פסוק and explains that צרעת softens the leather. The amud ends as רבא begins a new difficulty against his own view, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: All garments are included, but a freshly flayed hide is not
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא finishes its derivation: 'אשר עליה תכבס' includes every kind of garment, while the word 'בגד' excludes a hide that was only just flayed, since a garment means something that can already become טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Might you think all kinds of garments are included? The verse says 'that on which it is sprinkled, you shall launder.' Might you think I also include a hide right after it was flayed? The verse says 'garment': just as a garment is something that can become impure, so too anything that can become impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a ברייתא that reads the פסוק to decide which items need washing when blood of a חטאת lands on them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: First the ברייתא widens the rule: 'אשר עליה תכבס' covers every type of garment, not only wool or linen. Then it narrows the rule: the word 'בגד' teaches that the item must be like a garment, meaning something that can already become טמא. A hide that was only just flayed is not yet a finished item that can become טמא, so it is left out.

keyTerms.meaning: The verse says (introduces the פסוק that settles the question)
I include (widen the rule to cover)
After it was flayed (skinned off the animal)
An item that can already become ritually impure

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the key phrase 'דבר המקבל טומאה', which the rest of the section compares with the 'ראוי' view.

phrases.english: And all types of garments?
The verse says: 'That on which it is sprinkled, you shall launder.'
One might think that I include
a hide once it has been flayed?
The verse says 'garment':
just as a garment is an item that can become impure,
so too anything that can become impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא from the previous section of the daf.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: All garments require כיבוס, but only items already able to become טמא. A freshly flayed hide is excluded.

steps.title: What is the practical difference between the two views?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what practical case separates 'ראוי לטומאה' from 'דבר המקבל טומאה'.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difference between them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up the next move. It asks for a real-life case where the two views would give different results.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At first the two phrases sound the same: something 'fit' to become impure seems to be the same as something that 'can' become impure. The גמרא wants a concrete item that is fit but cannot yet actually become טמא.

keyTerms.meaning: What practical difference is there between the two opinions?

phrases.english: What is the difference between them?
phrases.notes: He means the view that says 'fit to become impure' and the view that says 'able to become impure.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how the 'מקבל טומאה' rule just derived differs from the 'ראוי' rule.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A concrete case where an item is ראוי לטומאה but is not yet מקבל טומאה.

steps.title: אביי: a cloth patch smaller than three fingerbreadths
steps.stepSummary: אביי says the difference is a small patch. It is 'fit' because its owner could designate it for use, but it cannot yet actually become טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: a patch smaller than three is the difference between them. The one who says 'fit' holds this is also fit, because if he wants he can designate it for a use. The one who says 'an item that can become impure' holds that this, at least, cannot become impure.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the question with a small scrap of cloth, smaller than three by three fingerbreadths.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A scrap this small cannot become טמא on its own. It becomes able to once the owner designates it for a use, such as patching a garment. Under the 'ראוי' view that possibility is enough, so it needs washing. Under the 'מקבל טומאה' view it does not need washing yet.

keyTerms.meaning: A patch or scrap of cloth
The one who says (the opinion that holds)
He designates it in his mind for a use

phrases.english: Abaye said:
A patch less than three
phrases.notes: He means three by three fingerbreadths. A scrap smaller than that does not normally become טמא.

phrases.english: is the difference between them.
The one who says 'fit':
this is also fit,
because if he wants, he can designate it.
phrases.notes: For example, he can decide to use it to patch a garment, and then it can become טמא.

phrases.english: The one who says 'an item that can become impure':

phrases.aramaic: הָא מִיהָא לָאו בַּת קַבּוֹלֵי טוּמְאָה הִיא.
phrases.english: this, at least, cannot become impure.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר אביי מטלית פחותה משלש איכא בינייהו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 2.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A patch smaller than three fingerbreadths needs washing under the 'ראוי' view, since designation could make it susceptible. It does not need washing under the 'מקבל טומאה' view.

steps.title: רבא: a garment meant to receive a picture
steps.stepSummary: רבא offers a different case: a garment the owner planned to decorate with a picture. It is unfinished and cannot yet become טמא, but he could cancel his plan.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: a garment on which he planned to put a picture is the difference between them. The one who says 'fit' holds this is also fit, because if he wants he can cancel his plan. The one who says 'an item that can become impure' holds that right now, at least, it cannot become impure.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives his own example of the practical difference between the two views.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the owner plans to add a picture, the garment counts as unfinished, so it cannot become טמא yet. Under the 'ראוי' view, he could drop the plan at any moment and it would be finished, so it needs washing now. Under the 'מקבל טומאה' view, all that matters is its status right now.

phrases.english: Rava said:
A garment on which he planned to put a picture
is the difference between them.
The one who says 'fit':
this is also fit,
because if he wants, he can cancel his plan.
The one who says 'an item that can become impure':

phrases.aramaic: הַשְׁתָּא מִיהָא לָאו בַּת קַבּוֹלֵי טוּמְאָה הִיא.
phrases.english: right now, at least, it cannot become impure.

steps.triggerLanguage: רבא אמר בגד שחישב עליה לצורה איכא בינייהו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second answer to step 2, alongside אביי's answer.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A garment meant for a picture needs washing under the 'ראוי' view, since the plan can be cancelled. It does not need washing under the 'מקבל טומאה' view.

steps.title: רבא, another version: an unfinished hide meant to be trimmed
steps.stepSummary: In another version רבא's case is an עוצבא, a raw hide the owner plans to trim. It cannot become טמא until it is trimmed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: an unfinished hide that he planned to trim is the difference between them. The one who says 'fit' holds this is also fit. The one who says 'an item that can become impure' holds it cannot become impure until he trims it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second version of what רבא said, using a leather hide instead of a cloth garment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: While the owner still plans to cut the hide to shape, it is not a finished item, so it cannot become טמא. Under the 'ראוי' view it needs washing, since he could drop the plan. Under the 'מקבל טומאה' view it does not, until the trimming is actually done.

keyTerms.meaning: To trim it (cut it to shape)

phrases.english: Rava said:
phrases.notes: This is a second version of what רבא said, not a new statement after the first one.

phrases.english: An unfinished hide that he planned to trim
is the difference between them.
The one who says 'fit':
this is also fit.
The one who says 'an item that can become impure':
this cannot become impure
until he trims it.

steps.confusionAlert: There are not two separate statements of רבא here. The second 'רבא אמר' is another version of the same teaching.
steps.triggerLanguage: רבא אמר עוצבא דחשיב עלה לקצעה איכא בינייהו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another version of רבא's answer from step 4.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: An untrimmed hide meant for trimming needs washing under the 'ראוי' view. It does not need washing under the 'מקבל טומאה' view until it is trimmed.

steps.title: Support: רבי שמעון בן מנסיא says the untrimmed hide stays pure
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא confirms the premise of רבא's second version: an עוצבא meant for trimming is טהור until it is trimmed.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it is taught in a ברייתא: רבי שמעון בן מנסיא says: an unfinished hide that he planned to trim is pure until he trims it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to back up the second version of רבא's case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's case only works if the untrimmed hide truly cannot become טמא yet. רבי שמעון בן מנסיא states exactly that: it stays טהור until it is trimmed. This shows the case really does separate 'fit' from 'can become impure.'
steps.whatToRemember: The 'ראוי' view requires washing anything that could become susceptible to טומאה. The 'מקבל טומאה' view requires washing only what is susceptible right now. The examples are a small patch (אביי), a garment meant for a picture (רבא), and an untrimmed hide (רבא's other version, supported by רבי שמעון בן מנסיא).

phrases.english: And it is taught:
Rabbi Shimon ben Menasya says:
An unfinished hide that he planned to trim
is pure until he trims it.

steps.triggerLanguage: והתניא רבי שמעון בן מנסיא אומר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the premise of step 5.
steps.raayaObject: That an untrimmed hide meant for trimming cannot yet become טמא, which is the premise of רבא's second version.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא of רבי שמעון בן מנסיא.

steps.title: Where do we learn that only the bloody spot needs laundering?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's rule that only the place of the blood needs laundering and asks for its source.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said the whole garment does not need laundering. Where do we learn this from?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to another line of the משנה and asks for the source. This is a setup question, and the answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה ruled that only the spot where blood landed must be washed, not the entire garment. The גמרא wants to know which פסוק teaches this limit.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know these things? (asking for a source)

phrases.english: [The whole garment] does not require laundering, etc.
From where are these matters derived?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the discussion of ראוי לטומאה to a new line of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source for limiting laundering to the bloody spot.

steps.title: A ברייתא learns it from the words 'that on which it shall be sprinkled'
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא reads the words ״אשר יזה״ as limiting laundering to the place of the blood.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: You might think that if blood sprayed on part of a garment, the whole garment needs laundering. So the פסוק says 'that on which it shall be sprinkled.' This means I only told you to wash the place of the blood.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question with a ברייתא that shows the source in the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא first suggests that the whole garment should need washing. It then rejects that idea from the extra words ״אשר יזה״, which point to the exact spot that was sprinkled. So the duty is limited to where the blood actually landed.

keyTerms.meaning: One might think (a possible mistake that is about to be rejected)
The פסוק teaches (introduces the correcting word)

phrases.english: As the Rabbis taught:
One might think: if it sprayed on part of a garment,
the whole garment should require laundering?
The verse says: 'that on which it shall be sprinkled' —
I did not tell you [to launder]
anything except the place of the blood alone.

steps.whatToRemember: Only the spot the blood touched needs laundering, learned from ״אשר יזה״.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the source question of step 7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The words ״אשר יזה״ limit laundering to the place of the blood.

steps.title: The unattributed משנה follows רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that the משנה's wording 'fit to become impure' matches רבי יהודה's view.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said 'an item that is fit to become impure.' This unnamed משנה follows רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the משנה's phrase and points out whose opinion it follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה requires laundering for anything 'fit' to become טמא, even if it cannot become טמא yet. That matches the wider rule of רבי יהודה. It does not match רבי אלעזר's narrower rule, which requires laundering only for an item that can actually become טמא now.

keyTerms.meaning: An unattributed (anonymous) statement in a משנה

phrases.english: 'An item that is fit to become impure,' etc.
phrases.notes: The word in square brackets ('etc.') is added in the corrected wording. It just signals that the quote continues.

phrases.english: The unattributed [משנה] is according to רבי יהודה.
phrases.notes: This connects back to the dispute behind steps 2–6: 'fit to become impure' versus 'actually able to become impure.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the ראוי לטומאה phrase discussed earlier and identifies its author.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה's 'fit to become impure' follows רבי יהודה.

steps.title: 'Fit for laundering' leaves out hard vessels
steps.stepSummary: The phrase 'fit for laundering' excludes a vessel, because blood is scraped off a vessel, not washed.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said 'fit for laundering.' This comes to exclude a vessel, since a vessel is something you scrape.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains what the phrase 'fit for laundering' comes to leave out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Laundering only fits materials that soak up blood, like cloth. A hard vessel does not absorb the blood, so you clean it by scraping. That is why vessels are not included in the duty of כיבוס.

phrases.english: 'Fit for laundering.'
This is to exclude a vessel,
since it is something [cleaned by] scraping.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues explaining the next phrase of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Vessels are not laundered. Blood on them is scraped off.

steps.title: Can leather really be laundered? A contradiction from a משנה about שבת
steps.stepSummary: The משנה includes leather in the duty of laundering, but a משנה about שבת lets you pour water on leather, as if washing leather is not laundering.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: a garment, sackcloth, and so on. Does this mean leather can be laundered? But there is a contradiction: if bird droppings were on a cushion, you wipe them with a rag. If the cushion was leather, you pour water on it until the droppings are gone!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה's assumption that leather can be laundered by quoting another משנה that seems to say the opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On שבת, washing cloth counts as laundering, which is forbidden, so you may only wipe it. Leather may be rinsed with water, which shows that washing leather is not considered 'laundering.' If so, how can our משנה require כיבוס for leather?

keyTerms.meaning: And they contrasted them (introduces a contradicting source)

steps.confusionAlert: The משנה about שבת is not about blood at all. It only matters because it shows how we view washing leather: as laundering or not.

phrases.english: 'Both a garment and sackcloth,' etc.
Is this to say that leather is suitable for laundering?!
And they raised a contradiction:
If there were bird droppings on it,
phrases.notes: 'It' is a cushion. This משנה is about cleaning things on שבת (שבת 142b).

phrases.english: he wipes it with a rag.
If it was on one of leather,
he puts water on it until it is gone!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next line of the משנה and attacks the assumption behind it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's inclusion of leather among items that require laundering.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה about שבת allows pouring water on leather, which shows that washing leather is not 'laundering'. That contradicts the idea that leather can be laundered.

steps.title: אביי: the two משניות follow different תנאים
steps.stepSummary: אביי resolves the contradiction by saying the משנה about שבת follows the רבנן and our משנה follows אחרים.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: It is not difficult. That משנה follows the רבנן, and this משנה follows אחרים.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the contradiction from step 11. He says the two משניות simply follow two different תנאים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is no real contradiction because two different opinions are speaking. The משנה about שבת, which treats water on leather as not laundering, follows the רבנן. Our משנה, which requires laundering leather, follows אחרים. The proof comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult; there is no real contradiction
'Others', a תנא quoted by this title

phrases.english: Abaye said: It is not difficult;
that one follows the Rabbis, this one follows Others.
phrases.notes: 'That one' is the משנה about שבת. 'This one' is our משנה about laundering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 11
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both משניות seemed to follow one view, so they contradicted each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: Each משנה follows a different תנא: the משנה about שבת follows the רבנן, and our משנה follows אחרים.

steps.title: The ברייתא showing the dispute about leather
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows that the רבנן put leather with vessels (scrape it), while אחרים put leather with garments (launder it).
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is taught: A garment or sackcloth, he launders it. A vessel or leather, he scrapes it. אחרים say: A garment, sackcloth, or leather, he launders it. A vessel, he scrapes it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to prove that אביי's מחלוקת really exists.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The only difference between the two opinions is leather. The רבנן group leather with a כלי, so blood is scraped off and washing it is not called laundering. אחרים group leather with cloth, so it must be laundered, just like our משנה says.
steps.whatToRemember: The whole argument is about leather: רבנן say scrape it like a vessel, אחרים say launder it like a garment.

phrases.english: As it is taught: A garment or sackcloth, he launders it;
a vessel or leather, he scrapes it.

phrases.aramaic: אֲחֵרִים אוֹמְרִים: הַבֶּגֶד וְהַשַּׂק וְהָעוֹר – מְכַבְּסוֹ,
phrases.english: Others say: A garment, sackcloth, or leather, he launders it;
and a vessel, he scrapes it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports אביי's answer with a ברייתא
steps.raayaObject: אביי's claim that there is a מחלוקת between רבנן and אחרים about leather
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about חטאת blood on garments, sackcloth, vessels, and leather

steps.title: Whose view fits רב חייא's story about רב's shoes?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which opinion matches רב חייא בר אשי's report that he often put water on רב's shoes.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view does this follow, what רב חייא בר אשי said: Many times I stood before רב and splashed water on his shoes?
steps.whatsHappening: Now that we know there is a מחלוקת, the גמרא asks which side fits a real-life story about רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חייא בר אשי poured water on רב's leather shoes on שבת, and רב did not object. That means רב did not treat it as laundering. The גמרא wants to know which תנא that matches.

phrases.english: Whose view does this follow,
that Rav Chiyya bar Ashi said:

phrases.aramaic: זִימְנִין סַגִּיאִין הֲוָה קָאֵימְנָא קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב,
phrases.english: Many times I would stand before Rav,
phrases.notes: This was on שבת, which is why it connects to the משנה about שבת.

phrases.english: and splash water on his shoes for him?

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּמַאן אָזְלָא הָא דְּאָמַר רַב חִיָּיא בַּר אָשֵׁי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the newly found מחלוקת to an אמורא's practice
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which side of the מחלוקת matches רב's practice of letting water be put on his leather shoes

steps.title: רב's practice follows the רבנן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רב's practice follows the רבנן, who hold leather is not laundered.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view? The רבנן's.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its own question: רב followed the רבנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן hold that washing leather is not laundering. So pouring water on leather shoes on שבת is no problem for them, and that is why רב allowed it.

keyTerms.meaning: Like the view of the Rabbis

phrases.english: Whose view? Like the Rabbis.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 14
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב's practice follows the רבנן of the ברייתא, for whom leather is not subject to laundering

steps.title: רבא: a verse says leather can be laundered
steps.stepSummary: רבא challenges אביי: how can anyone say leather cannot be laundered, when a פסוק about צרעת speaks of laundering leather?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Is there anyone who says leather is not fit for laundering? But it is written: 'And the garment, or the warp, or the woof, or any article of leather that you shall wash'!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא attacks אביי's answer. He says no תנא could hold that leather cannot be laundered, because the תורה says it can.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי's answer depends on the רבנן saying leather is never laundered. But the פסוק in the laws of צרעת clearly says 'any article of leather that you shall wash'. So the רבנן's view, as אביי explained it, seems to go against a פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: Is there anyone who says...? (a strong objection)

phrases.english: Rava said:
And is there anyone who says
that leather is not fit for laundering?!
But isn't it written:
"And the garment, or the warp, or the woof,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ כׇל כְּלִי הָעוֹר אֲשֶׁר תְּכַבֵּס״!
phrases.english: or any article of leather that you shall wash"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back and challenges אביי's answer itself
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's reading that the רבנן hold leather is never subject to laundering
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A פסוק explicitly speaks of laundering leather, so no תנא could hold leather is never launderable.

steps.title: רבא: soft leather versus hard leather
steps.stepSummary: רבא gives his own answer: the פסוק and our משנה speak of soft leather, and the רבנן and אחרים argue only about hard leather.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: The verse and our משנה are about soft leather. When they argue, it is about hard leather.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא replaces אביי's answer with a new one. Everyone agrees soft leather can be laundered; the argument is only about hard leather.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This keeps everyone in line with the פסוק. Soft leather is like cloth, so the פסוק and our משנה require laundering it. Hard leather is like a vessel, and only about that do the רבנן say 'scrape it' while אחרים say 'launder it'.
steps.whatToRemember: According to רבא, soft leather is launderable according to everyone; only hard leather is in dispute.
steps.confusionAlert: רבא does not say the רבנן and אחרים agree. They still argue, but only about hard leather.

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said:
The verse and our Mishnah are about soft ones,
when they argue, it is about hard ones.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a new answer after rejecting אביי's
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting between cases (soft vs. hard leather)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The רבנן seemed to say all leather is never laundered, which goes against the פסוק.
steps.terutzMaskana: Soft leather is launderable according to everyone; the מחלוקת is only about hard leather.

steps.title: Challenge from רב's shoes
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבא with רב חייא's story: רב's shoes were washed on שבת, yet shoes are leather that should be launderable.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't רב חייא say: Many times I stood before רב and splashed water on his shoes!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings back the story about רב's shoes as a challenge to רבא's new answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If soft leather can be laundered according to everyone, then washing leather shoes on שבת should be forbidden laundering. Yet רב allowed it, so it seems to clash with רבא.

phrases.english: But didn't Rav Chiyya say:
phrases.notes: This is the same רב חייא בר אשי from step 14.

phrases.aramaic: זִימְנִין סַגִּיאִין הֲוָה קָאֵימְנָא קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב,
phrases.english: Many times I would stand before Rav,
and splash water on his shoes for him!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's answer
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's claim that soft leather is launderable according to everyone
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Leather shoes were washed on שבת with רב's approval, which would be forbidden if leather counts as launderable.

steps.title: רב's shoes were hard leather, following the רבנן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רב's shoes were made of hard leather, and he followed the רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: They were hard ones, and רב followed the רבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge in two words: the shoes were hard leather, and רב held like the רבנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For hard leather there is a מחלוקת, and the רבנן say washing it is not laundering. So רב, following the רבנן, could allow water on his hard leather shoes on שבת. רבא's answer stands.
steps.whatToRemember: רבא's answer holds: soft leather is launderable, and רב's hard shoes followed the רבנן's lenient view about hard leather.

phrases.english: It was about hard ones, and like the Rabbis.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 18
steps.terutzResolutionType: Defining the case (the shoes were hard leather)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב's shoes seemed to be soft leather, which everyone agrees is launderable.
steps.terutzMaskana: The shoes were hard leather, and רב followed the רבנן who say hard leather is not laundered.

steps.title: רבא takes back his own answer
steps.stepSummary: רבא rejects his earlier claim that the צרעת פסוק speaks only of soft leather. The פסוק also covers hard imported leather, and it still requires laundering.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא then said: What I said is not right. Should we really claim the פסוק only means soft leather? The פסוק also covers hard leather items brought from overseas, and the Torah still says they need laundering.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא knocks down his own earlier answer from Step 17. He says you cannot limit the פסוק to soft leather only.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 17, רבא said the צרעת פסוק is about soft leather, so it does not touch the argument about hard leather. Now he points out that the פסוק says leather in general, which includes hard leather like the imported kind. The Torah still requires laundering there, so his limit on the פסוק does not work.

keyTerms.meaning: He then said (he changes his mind about what he said before)
What I said is not correct

steps.confusionAlert: Here רבא is attacking his own earlier answer, not someone else's. 'הדר' tells you he is taking back what he said before.

phrases.english: Rava then said:
What I said is not correct;
phrases.notes: He means his answer from before: that the פסוק speaks only of soft leather.

phrases.english: shall we stand and say of the verse
that when [leather items] are written, they are written about soft ones?!
Are we not dealing also
with hard leather items
that come from overseas,
and the Merciful One says they need laundering?
phrases.notes: This is the צרעת פסוק about laundering a leather item, ויקרא 13:58.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲדַר אָמַר רָבָא: לָאו מִילְּתָא הִיא דַּאֲמַרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to רבא's answer in Step 17 and rejects it.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: רבא's reading that the צרעת פסוק speaks only of soft leather.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The פסוק speaks of leather in general, which includes hard imported leather, and it still requires laundering.

steps.title: Leprosy softens the leather
steps.stepSummary: רבא gives a new answer. צרעת grows out of the item itself and loosens it, so even hard leather with צרעת becomes soft.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: With צרעת, since it sprouts out of the item itself, it loosens the leather and makes it soft.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a new way to explain the פסוק. He agrees it can be about hard leather, but says צרעת makes that leather soft.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק requires laundering even for hard leather, but only once it has צרעת. Because the צרעת grows from inside the item, it loosens the leather and turns it soft. So the פסוק does not prove that ordinary hard leather can be laundered, and the argument between the רבנן and אחרים about hard leather still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: The צרעת affliction that can appear on clothing and leather

steps.whatToRemember: Hard leather is still hard leather. The צרעת case is a special exception, because the צרעת itself softens it. So the פסוק cannot settle the argument about ordinary hard leather.
steps.whyThisMatters: This keeps the argument between the רבנן and אחרים alive. It also keeps the earlier answer about רב's hard-leather shoes from Step 19 standing.

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said:
Leprosy, since it sprouts from the item itself,
it loosens it
and makes it soft.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the answer that רבא rejected in Step 20 with a new answer to the question from Step 16.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Special-case explanation: the case in the פסוק is different because of what צרעת does to leather.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the פסוק includes hard leather, it seemed to prove that all hard leather can be laundered.
steps.terutzMaskana: The hard leather in the פסוק has become soft because of the צרעת, so it proves nothing about ordinary hard leather.

steps.title: רבא introduces his own difficulty
steps.stepSummary: רבא announces that one thing still troubles him about his own view. This sets up the question that comes next.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: If something bothers me, this is what bothers me:
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. רבא is about to raise a difficulty against his own view that everyone agrees soft leather can be laundered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא has just defended his view, but he admits one point still bothers him. The actual difficulty is not in this line. It comes right after, in the next part of the גמרא.

keyTerms.term: אִי קַשְׁיָא לִי, הָא קַשְׁיָא לִי
keyTerms.meaning: If something is difficult for me, this is what is difficult for me

phrases.english: Rava said:

phrases.aramaic: אִי קַשְׁיָא לִי, הָא קַשְׁיָא לִי:
phrases.english: If something is difficult for me, this is what is difficult for me:

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי קַשְׁיָא לִי, הָא קַשְׁיָא לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After defending his view, רבא begins to raise a new difficulty against it.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's own view that everyone agrees soft leather can be laundered.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Not yet stated. This line only introduces the difficulty that follows.
